schema_notes.fill_price_convention: THE FILL IS THE BROKER'S 'Net Prc' COLUMN, NEVER amount/shares. Settled 2026-08-26 after the two disagreed on every recent paste. amount/shares is the LIMIT notional; Net Prc is the executed share-weighted average, and a limit fills AT OR BETTER than its limit — which is why Net Prc is favourable in BOTH directions (FANG sell 197.72 > 197.0000; EQT buy 53.8559 < 53.9600). The decisive evidence is decimal places: EQT's 53.8559 carries FOUR, and a US equity limit cannot, because the minimum tick is $0.01 — so it can only be an average of executions, while 197.0000 and 53.9600 are exact to the cent, as limits are. NOTE ON PROVENANCE: no broker statement exists on this machine (searched Downloads/Desktop/Documents), so this was adjudicated from the arithmetic above plus minute bars, NOT read off a statement. It is a reasoned convention, not a documented one. WHY IT MATTERS: realized_r is stored RECOMPUTABLE from the stored entry_stop, so a limit-derived price stores a wrong R against a correct stop. FANG would have been recorded -0.9506R instead of -0.8137R.

schema_notes.benchmarks: Two, never conflated. The DOCTRINE's modelled fill is the NEXT OPEN after the trigger close (grade_outcomes.py takes df['Open'].iloc[fired_i+1]). The CLOSE-BASIS ESTIMATE is the value at the trigger close and is an ESTIMATE (notify_assessment.py renders it as basis: close_estimate). Execution shortfall splits into GAP (trigger close -> next open) and DELAY (next open -> actual fill).
